literal: When Wenxuan received the Mandate, Sihao was made Grand General of the Left Guard.
idiomatic: When Wenxuan took the throne, Sihao was made grand general of the Left Guard.

literal: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, campaigning against the Rouran, Wenxuan was pleased with his fierce valor and said: "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — you ought to think of good deeds.
idiomatic: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, on campaign against the Rouran, Wenxuan delighted in his fierce bravery and said, "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — think on deeds worthy of that gift.

literal: " Hence he was renamed.
idiomatic: " Hence his name was changed.

literal: He rose in succession to Director of the Masters of Writing, Field Headquarters of the Shuozhou Circuit, Governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment, and Prince of Nan'an — and won the hearts of the northern frontier greatly.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to director of the Masters of Writing, field headquarters of the Shuozhou circuit, governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment honors, and Prince of Nan'an — and won deep loyalty on the northern frontier.

literal: In the time of the Later Lord, Zhuogu Guangbian came on mission to the province; Sihao received him with great courtesy, but Guangbian was arrogant and haughty — Sihao therefore nursed resentment in his heart.
idiomatic: Under the Later Lord, Zhuogu Guangbian came to the province on mission. Sihao received him with scrupulous courtesy; Guangbian repaid him with arrogance — and Sihao nursed the insult in silence.

literal: In the fifth year of Wuping, he thereupon raised troops in rebellion.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuping he rose in arms.

literal: He wrote to the nobles of Bing Province: "Our lord grew up deep in the palace and cannot distinguish true from false in men; he draws close to the vicious and cunning and keeps the loyal and good at a distance.
idiomatic: He wrote the nobles of Bing Province: "Our lord was reared deep in the palace and cannot tell sincerity from deceit. He cleaves to the vicious and shuns the loyal.

literal: Thus eunuchs mutilated by blade and saw overflow the steps of the hall; vile merchant-Hu grasp power within the curtains, stripping the living and plundering the markets of the court.
idiomatic: Eunuchs mutilated by blade and saw now crowd the palace steps; foul merchant-adventurers hold the reins within the curtains — stripping the people bare and pillaging the court itself.

literal: Dull in hearing and accepting counsel, he devotes himself to cruel harm.
idiomatic: Deaf to remonstrance, he delights in cruelty.

literal: He shuts his mother deep in the palace and no longer keeps a son's rites;
idiomatic: He has locked his mother away in the inner palace and cast off a son's duty;

literal: his two younger brothers were slaughtered — the bond of flesh and bone was severed at a stroke.
idiomatic: his two younger brothers were butchered — the bond of flesh and blood cut off in a stroke.

literal: He still indulges Zili in seizing horses at the eastern gate, Guangbian in carrying falcons at the western market — Bolo receives the title Equal in Protocol, Xiaoyao the name Lady of the Commandery; dogs and horses take rank alongside men, their glory topping the court caps and sashes.
idiomatic: He indulges Zili seizing horses at the eastern gate, Guangbian strutting with falcons at the western market — Bolo granted protocol equal to princes, Xiaoyao styled lady of a commandery. Dogs and horses take rank beside men; their glory outshines court caps and robes.

literal: The people cannot bear the burdens; they long for chaos to end.
idiomatic: The people buckle under their burdens and pray for an end to this disorder.

literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the clan's flower — the altars rest upon him alone. Left Chancellor Hulü Guang mingled the moon, for generations a chief minister, his might famed among neighboring states — yet innocent of guilt, he was suddenly put to death.
idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the flower of the clan — upon him alone the altars rest. Left Chancellor Hulü Guang mingled the moon, chief minister through generations, his renown ringing in every neighboring realm — and yet, guiltless, he was suddenly destroyed.

literal: I, unworthy though I am to share the imperial branch, have truly received extraordinary favor — now I shall lead righteous troops to strike down the harm at the ruler's side.
idiomatic: Unworthy as I am of the imperial branch, I have nonetheless received extraordinary favor. Today I lead righteous troops to purge the evil at our lord's side.

literal: I pray you understand this heart and harbor no doubt.
idiomatic: Know my heart in this, and lend no ear to doubt.

literal: " — the words of Field Headquarters Attendant Wang Xingsi.
idiomatic: " — penned by field headquarters attendant Wang Xingsi.

literal: Sihao reached Yangqu, styled himself Grand Chancellor, set up all the hundred officials, and made Left Assistant of the Field Headquarters Wang Shangzhi his chief clerk.
idiomatic: Sihao reached Yangqu and styled himself grand chancellor. He set up a full bureaucracy and made left assistant of the field headquarters Wang Shangzhi his chief clerk.

literal: Guard General Zhao Hai held troops at Jinyang; pressed for time and unable to memorialize, he forged an edict and mobilized troops to resist.
idiomatic: Guard general Zhao Hai held the soldiers at Jinyang. With no time to report upward, he forged an edict and mobilized the troops to resist.

literal: The soldiers all said: "The Prince of Nan'an is coming — we need only shout ten thousand years and welcome him.
idiomatic: The soldiers said among themselves, "Prince of Nan'an is coming — we need only shout 'ten thousand years!' and welcome him.

literal: " The emperor heard of the uprising and sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and Central Army Commander Kudi Shiwen galloping to Jinyang; the emperor himself led troops and followed after.
idiomatic: " Learning of the revolt, the emperor sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and central army commander Kudi Shiwen racing to Jinyang, while he himself led troops in pursuit.

literal: Sihao's army was defeated; he and Xingsi threw themselves into the water and died.
idiomatic: Sihao's army collapsed. He and Xingsi cast themselves into the water and drowned.

literal: His two thousand followers — Taozhi besieged them, killing and summoning by turns; in the end none surrendered, and all perished.
idiomatic: Taozhi surrounded his two thousand followers, killing and calling them to surrender in turn. None yielded, and all were killed to the last man.

literal: The emperor was on the road; Chinu Shi'an carried the victory bulletin from Jinyang toward Pingdu and encountered Husixiao Xiaoqing.
idiomatic: The emperor was still on the march when Chinu Shi'an set out from Jinyang bearing the victory bulletin toward Pingdu — and met Husixiao Xiaoqing on the way.

literal: Xiaoqing tempted him to eat, then galloped on to the traveling palace and cried out that all was settled.
idiomatic: Xiaoqing lured him to sit and eat, then raced ahead to the traveling palace and cried out that the matter was finished.

literal: The emperor rejoiced greatly; those at his side shouted ten thousand years.
idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed; his attendants shouted "Ten thousand years!"

literal: After a long while Shi'an at last made his report of what had occurred.
idiomatic: Only after a long interval did Shi'an arrive and explain what had happened.

literal: The emperor said: "What manner of victory bulletin is this, that you could sit down and eat?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "What sort of bulletin permits a man to stop and dine?

literal: " Thereupon he rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an's offense.
idiomatic: " He rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an.

literal: Sihao's corpse was displayed for seven days, then flayed, butchered, and burned; Shangzhi was boiled alive at the Ye market; palace eunuchs were ordered to shoot Sihao's consort within the palace, then burn her to death.
idiomatic: Sihao's corpse was put on display seven days, then butchered, skinned, and burned. Shangzhi was boiled alive in the Ye market. Palace eunuchs were told to shoot Sihao's consort inside the palace — then burn what remained.

literal: Fifty days before Sihao's rebellion someone reported his plot.
idiomatic: Fifty days before the revolt, someone denounced Sihao for plotting rebellion.

literal: Han Changluan's daughter was married to Sihao's son — he therefore memorialized that someone was slandering the nobles, that the affair was stirring disturbance, and that unless the informant were killed there could be no peace afterward; the man was beheaded.
idiomatic: Han Changluan's daughter was married to Sihao's son. He memorialized that the report was slander meant to unsettle the nobles — that unless the informant were killed, trouble would follow. The man was beheaded.

literal: After Sihao was put to death, the dead informant's younger brother prostrated himself below the palace gate, pleading that his brother be posthumously honored; Changluan would not relay the petition.
idiomatic: After Sihao's death, the informant's younger brother lay prostrate below the palace gate, begging posthumous honors for his brother. Changluan refused to pass the petition.

literal: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger clansman of Shenwu on the father's side.
idiomatic: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger cousin of Gao Huan.

literal: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and sentenced to exile in Liangzhou; traveling between the Yellow and Wei rivers he encountered bandits and, through military merit, obtained release from banishment.
idiomatic: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and condemned to exile in Liangzhou. Between the Yellow and Wei rivers he met bandits and, through military service, won release from banishment.

literal: He therefore remained in Hezhou many years.
idiomatic: He remained in Hezhou many years.

literal: Because he understood the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and for merit was made Governor of Hedong.
idiomatic: Fluent in the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and was made governor of Hedong for his merit.

literal: Before long he died there.
idiomatic: He died there not long after.

literal: Hui and Shenwu had been bound by deep old obligation.
idiomatic: Hui and Gao Huan shared a deep old bond.

literal: When Shenwu pacified the capital and Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin back and buried him in the same tomb precinct as Lady Mu.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan pacified Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin home and buried him in the same tomb compound as Lady Mu.

literal: Hui was posthumously made Minister over the Masses, posthumous name Wensuan.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister over the masses, posthumous name Wensuan.

literal: At first, when the Prince of Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed the edict and left five thousand troops of the imperial escort in the Western Quarter, secretly preparing against the unexpected.
idiomatic: When Prince of Jinan first traveled from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin read the edict leaving five thousand troops of the escort in the Western Quarter — a secret guard against surprise.

literal: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it — and from this nursed secret resentment against Yang and Yan.
idiomatic: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it and began to nurse secret resentment against Yang and Yan.

literal: Yang, Yan, and the rest wished to remove the two princes and asked Guiyan's counsel.
idiomatic: Yang, Yan, and their faction meant to remove the two princes and sought Guiyan's counsel.

literal: Guiyan feigned delight and asked to take counsel together with Yuanhai.
idiomatic: Guiyan feigned enthusiasm and proposed consulting Yuanhai together.

literal: Yuanhai likewise assented with his mouth while his heart refused, and galloped to inform Prince of Changguang.
idiomatic: Yuanhai agreed with his lips while his heart refused, and raced to warn Prince of Changguang.

literal: Prince of Changguang thereupon put Yang, Yan, and the rest to death.
idiomatic: Changguang thereupon executed Yang, Yan, and their allies.

literal: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, Commander Cheng Xiuning drew up troops and barred him; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then was entry granted — proceeding toward the Cypress Pavilion and the Eternal Lane, the same again.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, commander Cheng Xiuning drew up his troops and barred the way. Guiyan talked him round — only then was entry granted. The same at Cypress Pavilion and Eternal Lane.

literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, for this he was all the more favored and honored — whenever he entered audience he was always ranked above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, Guiyan was favored all the more for this — at every audience he was seated above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.

literal: He was made Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was made minister of works and concurrently director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Under Qi law, within the palace only the Son of Heaven wore the gauze cap; all subjects wore military caps — Guiyan was specially granted a gauze cap as a mark of favor.
idiomatic: Under Qi law only the emperor wore the gauze cap within the palace; all others wore military caps. Guiyan alone was granted a gauze cap — a singular mark of favor.

literal: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng at Ye.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng to Ye.

literal: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was advanced to Grand Tutor, held the title Minister over the Masses, and was regularly permitted to bring three private retainers, swords at belt, into the guard of honor.
idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was made grand tutor and minister over the masses, and was regularly allowed three armed retainers at his side in the guard of honor.

literal: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the high nobles all vied to invite him — wherever he went, the whole gathering leaned toward him.
idiomatic: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the great families vied to host him. Wherever he went, the room tilted his way.

literal: Guiyan now stood among generals and chancellors; his ambition brimmed over — his words were overbearing and insulting, as if no one else were present.
idiomatic: Having reached the summit of general and chancellor, Guiyan's ambition brimmed over. His speech turned overbearing, as though no one else were in the room.

literal: Commentators held that his might and authority alarmed the ruler — he would surely bring calamity and chaos.
idiomatic: Commentators warned that his power overshadowed the throne — disaster was inevitable.

literal: The emperor also traced his earlier shifts of loyalty and gradually grew wary.
idiomatic: The emperor, recalling his earlier betrayals, grew wary.

literal: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly spoke of his faults.
idiomatic: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly denounced him.

literal: The emperor visited Guiyan's home, summoned Wei Shou to compose an edict in the royal presence, intending to add the title Right Chancellor.
idiomatic: The emperor visited Guiyan's home and summoned Wei Shou to draft an edict in his presence — intending to add the title right chancellor.

literal: Shou said to Yuanhai: "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor — now, because Guiyan's fame and power are too great, he is being sent out; how could that title be given again?
idiomatic: Shou said to Yuanhai, "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor. Guiyan's fame is too great — that is why he is being sent away. How can we give him that title again?

literal: " He was therefore appointed Grand Preceptor and Governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied it out at once.
idiomatic: " Instead he was appointed grand preceptor and governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied the edict at once.

literal: That same day, an order was issued to the gate office forbidding entry into the palace without permission.
idiomatic: That same day an order went to the gate office: no entry to the palace without leave.

literal: Guiyan was at home drinking freely; he knew nothing until dawn. When he wished to attend audience and reached the gate and learned of it, he was greatly startled and withdrew.
idiomatic: Guiyan was at home drinking through the night and knew nothing. At dawn he set out for audience — reached the gate, learned what had happened, and fled back in alarm.

literal: When he announced himself to take leave, he was ordered to depart early; money, silk, musicians, and medicine were separately bestowed — every need provided.
idiomatic: When he announced himself to take leave, he was told to depart at once. Money, silk, musicians, physicians — every comfort was provided.

literal: Military officers and commanders were also ordered to escort him all the way to Qingyang Palace; they bowed and withdrew, none daring to speak with him together.
idiomatic: Military officers were ordered to escort him to Qingyang Palace. They bowed and withdrew — none dared speak with him.

literal: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he converse at length — at the time none overheard them.
idiomatic: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he speak at length — and no one heard what passed.

literal: Reaching the province, he could not feel secure; he plotted rebellion — intending to wait until the transfer of authority was complete, distribute rewards to the soldiers, watch for the imperial carriage to go to Jinyang, and seize Ye while it was empty.
idiomatic: At his province he could not rest easy. He plotted rebellion — waiting until his transfer was complete, rewarding the troops, watching for the emperor's journey to Jinyang, then seizing Ye while the capital lay open.

literal: He was denounced by his chief clerk of the prince's household Lü Sili; an edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to strike him.
idiomatic: His chief clerk Lü Sili denounced him. An edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to move against him.

literal: Guiyan had long maintained private relay stations on the southern border; hearing that troops were pressing near, he sent word ahead and immediately closed the city and defended it.
idiomatic: Guiyan had long kept private courier stations on the southern border. Hearing that troops were closing in, he sent word ahead and shut himself within the city walls.

literal: Earlier, Chief Clerk of Ji Province Yuwen Zhongluan, Administrator Li Zuyi, Aide Chen Jiqiong, Attendant Fang Zibi, and Administrator of Changle Commandery Wei Puxing and others had suspected Guiyan of disloyalty and jointly sent a secret memorial — Guiyan pursued and captured them, then imprisoned Zhongluan and the other five; they still would not submit, and all were killed.
idiomatic: Earlier, Ji Province chief clerk Yuwen Zhongluan, administrator Li Zuyi, aide Chen Jiqiong, attendant Fang Zibi, and Changle commandery administrator Wei Puxing had suspected Guiyan of treachery and sent a joint secret memorial. Guiyan pursued and captured them, imprisoned all five — and when they still refused to yield, killed them.

literal: The army had already pressed the walls; Guiyan mounted the ramparts and shouted: "When Emperor Xiaozhao first died, the six armies and a million soldiers all passed through my hands — I threw myself into going to Ye to welcome Your Majesty; I did not rebel then — how could I harbor a different heart today?
idiomatic: The army was at the walls. Guiyan mounted the ramparts and shouted, "When Emperor Xiaozhao died, a million soldiers passed through my hands. I raced to Ye to welcome Your Majesty — I did not rebel then. Why would my heart be different now?

literal: I only resent Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe for deceiving the sage ruler and envying and destroying the loyal and good.
idiomatic: I resent only Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe — they deceive the throne and destroy the loyal.

literal: Kill these three men and I will come before the walls and cut my own throat.
idiomatic: Kill these three and I will come before the walls and cut my own throat.

literal: " Afterward the city fell; he fled north alone on horseback, reached Jiaojin, was captured, and was chained and sent to Ye.
idiomatic: " The city fell. He fled north alone on horseback, was taken at Jiaojin, chained, and sent to Ye.

literal: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui question him privately as to his reasons.
idiomatic: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui question him in private.

literal: Guiyan said: "To let yellow-chinned boys drag me about — how could I not rebel!
idiomatic: Guiyan said, "Yellow-chinned boys dragging me about — how could I not rebel!

literal: " He asked: "Who?
idiomatic: " Rui asked, "Who?

literal: " Guiyan said: "Yuanhai and Qianhe — are they venerable elders of the court?
idiomatic: " Guiyan said, "Yuanhai and Qianhe — are they venerable elders of the court?

literal: In the days of the Zhao family's old lord, would I have nursed resentment?
idiomatic: In the days of the Zhao family's old lord, would I have nursed resentment?

literal: " The emperor then sent men to rebuke him further.
idiomatic: " The emperor sent men to rebuke him again.

literal: He replied: "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's mansion and used it as his own provincial seat, and was given rear-guard musicians.
idiomatic: He replied, "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's mansion for his provincial seat and was given rear-guard musicians.

literal: I am a frontier prince and grand preceptor — yet I still may not have musicians.
idiomatic: I am a frontier prince and grand preceptor — and still I may not have musicians.

literal: I would kill only Yuanhai and Yiyun.
idiomatic: I would kill only Yuanhai and Yiyun.

literal: " The emperor ordered Commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in; Guiyan still spoke as before, hoping to live.
idiomatic: " The emperor ordered commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in. Guiyan still spoke as before, hoping to live.

literal: The emperor commanded that his crime be deliberated; all said he could not be pardoned.
idiomatic: The emperor commanded deliberation on his crime. All agreed he could not be pardoned.

literal: He was loaded onto an open cart, a gag in his mouth, face bound; Liu Taozhi held a blade over him, drums beating as they went — he and fifteen descendants were all executed in the market.
idiomatic: He was loaded onto an open cart, gagged and bound. Liu Taozhi held a blade over him while drums beat along the route — he and fifteen descendants were all executed in the market.

literal: Posthumously he was made Governor of Renzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Renzhou.

literal: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were obtained, stored in the armory.
idiomatic: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were found and stored in the armory.

literal: Wenxuan entered the storehouse to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.
idiomatic: Wenxuan entered the armory to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.

literal: He said: "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled — when you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han.
idiomatic: He said, "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled. When you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han.

literal: " Guiyan had three ridges on his forehead bone; wearing a headcloth he could not keep it in place.
idiomatic: " Guiyan had three ridges on his brow; a headcloth would not sit straight on his skull.

literal: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry; he had him struck on the forehead with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying: "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han.
idiomatic: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry. He had Guiyan struck on the brow with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying, "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han.

literal: " His words of rebellion were fulfilled in the end.
idiomatic: " In the end his words of rebellion came true.

literal: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.
idiomatic: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.

literal: By nature he was generous, harmonious, and possessed of measure.
idiomatic: By nature he was generous, even-tempered, and possessed of measure.

literal: At nine years of age, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang together with him, Shenwu had him lodge and roam with his own sons.
idiomatic: At nine, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang with him, Gao Huan had him lodge and roam with his own sons.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

literal: In the second year of Wuping he rose in succession to Minister of Works.
idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he rose to minister of works.

literal: In the sixth year he was made Field Headquarters of the Yuzhou Circuit and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made field headquarters of the Yuzhou circuit and director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made grand preceptor.
